vibe: Patch pressure meets an AI market in fast motion: emergency Brotli fixes, live PHP2Shell exploitation, Anthropic's IPO and a surprise new OpenAI model lead the day.

cyber.title: Critical HTTP2Shell Brotli vulnerability triggers emergency patches
cyber.summary: A critical Brotli flaw is driving emergency remediation across affected stacks, including follow-up fixes from PHP and Microsoft .NET. Inventory exposed services and apply vendor patches promptly rather than assuming an earlier update fully covered the issue.

cyber.title: PHP2Shell security flaws now successfully exploited in the wild
cyber.summary: Researchers report successful real-world exploitation of the PHP2Shell flaws. Internet-facing PHP systems need immediate patch verification, exposure review and log hunting for exploitation attempts.

cyber.title: Attackers use Microsoft Teams IT-support scams to deploy ransomware
cyber.summary: Attackers are impersonating IT support through Microsoft Teams and turning social engineering into malware and ransomware delivery. Tighten external-chat controls, reinforce help-desk verification and brief staff that a Teams call is not proof of identity.

cyber.title: LiteLLM says an unrevoked key let hackers target users
cyber.summary: LiteLLM says attackers abused a key that had not been revoked, underscoring how AI gateways concentrate credentials and blast radius. Rotate secrets, audit access paths and treat model-routing infrastructure as production security infrastructure.

cyber.title: Malicious Downloads file tricks an AI coding agent into installing malware
cyber.summary: A hostile local instruction file can be mistaken for trusted agent guidance and lead a coding assistant toward malware installation. Keep untrusted downloads out of agent search paths and inspect inherited instruction files before granting tool access.

cyber.title: DreamHost forces password resets during an ongoing incident
cyber.summary: DreamHost is forcing email, FTP and SFTP credential resets while investigating an incident. Customers should reset unique credentials, rotate any reused secrets and monitor hosted assets for unusual changes.

cyber.title: Microsoft 365 token-replay attacks compromise 97 accounts at 79 organisations
cyber.summary: A token-replay campaign reportedly compromised 97 accounts across 79 organisations. Review risky sign-ins and session activity, revoke suspect tokens and make phishing-resistant authentication the target state.

cyber.title: Gheist weaponises GitHub tokens to steal cloud secrets
cyber.summary: The Gheist campaign uses stolen GitHub tokens as a route to cloud credentials and secrets. Minimise token scope, expire credentials aggressively and scan repositories plus CI logs for secret access anomalies.

ai.title: OpenAI introduces GPT-6.1 Terra
ai.summary: OpenAI's new GPT-6.1 Terra release immediately drew strong developer attention. The practical questions are capability gains, pricing and migration behaviour; treat early benchmark claims as provisional until independent testing lands.

ai.title: Anthropic formally files for an IPO
ai.summary: Anthropic's S-1 turns one of AI's most closely watched private companies into a public-market story, exposing more of its finances, risk posture and enterprise strategy. The filing also foregrounds catastrophic-risk language unusual for a major technology flotation.

ai.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut LLM prices by up to 80% — here's why
ai.summary: A widely discussed analysis examines the rapid collapse in frontier-model pricing. Better inference efficiency and competitive pressure are making ambitious agent workflows cheaper, but volatile pricing strengthens the case for model abstraction and cost telemetry.

ai.title: Tsinghua open-sources AKV, a cache server for LLM agents on SGLang
ai.summary: AKV targets reuse and engineering of key-value caches for agent workloads on SGLang. It is a technically relevant infrastructure release for teams trying to cut latency and inference cost across repeated, context-heavy calls.

ai.title: Europe's open-source LLM gateway aims to tame token bills
ai.summary: An open-source gateway proposal focuses on routing and controlling model spend. It fits a growing enterprise need for provider portability, policy enforcement and reliable per-workload token accounting.

ai.title: Nanbeige4.3-33B arrives as an open agentic coding model
ai.summary: The 33B open model targets coding-agent work at a size that may be practical for private deployment. Independent evaluations and tool-use reliability matter more than launch benchmarks, but it is one to watch for local stacks.

it.title: Microsoft offers mass buyouts to roughly a quarter of its workforce
it.summary: Microsoft is reportedly offering broad buyouts covering roughly a quarter of staff. The scale makes this a significant industry signal about cost structure and how AI investment is reshaping headcount priorities.

it.title: Work accelerates on protecting DNS from quantum decryption
it.summary: Standards and implementation work around post-quantum DNS protection is gathering pace. It is not an overnight migration, but infrastructure teams should begin tracking dependencies and crypto-agility plans now.

videos.title: This 3 trillion parameter model should be impossible...
videos.verdict: WATCH — concise, entertaining orientation to Kimi K3.1 and why its open-model benchmark results matter.
videos.summary: Fireship reviews Moonshot's three-trillion-parameter Kimi K3.1, its frontier-level coding benchmarks and the unresolved distillation debate. A hands-on 3D-generation test finds impressive output but weaker animation structure than proprietary frontier models.

videos.title: Agentic Engineering: 5 Terms Every AI Developer Should Know
videos.verdict: SKIM — useful vocabulary refresher; the middle section on context, harnesses and loops carries most of the value.
videos.summary: A clear primer spanning prompt and context engineering, harnesses, agent loops, graph orchestration and software factories. It stresses isolation, identity and observability as the operational basics for multi-agent development.

videos.title: Spotify's infrastructure runs faster on Google Cloud Axion
videos.verdict: SKIM — short customer case study, useful mainly for the scale and migration figures.
videos.summary: Spotify says its Arm-based Axion migration delivered roughly 2.5x performance and more than 40% price-performance savings across a huge Java-and-Kubernetes estate. The video is promotional, but the claimed ease of an architecture change at 1.5–2 million cores is notable.
